rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, and nothing has been run yet, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing.

What this document declares, before anything has been run. "0 functions promise nothing" counts functions that end up with nothing checked -- whether nobody wrote any checks for them, or the document switched checking off for them on purpose. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.

component ring — maps to Rust module disruptor::spsc capabilities: unsafe owns disruptor::spsc::Spsc — only this component may mutate them profile hot_path — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn; none of it has been run yet this box is this shade because `slot` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

this component may use `unsafe`. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — that limit is declared here, and not checked by this build: Ply currently compares crate-level dependencies and does not yet look inside functions, so use of a capability this component never declared can still go unnoticed (§5.3)

profile `hot_path` — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly)

slot bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times mutate — plants small deliberate bugs; the test/fuzz checks must catch every one, or the contract is flagged weak fuzz(4096) — runs the function on 4096 random inputs, checking the contract on each
Spsc::with_capacity bounded(2) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 2 times generic — every check runs with T=u64; whatever they earn covers only that type

Spsc::try_push bounded(3) — proves the contract for every input, unrolling loops at most 3 times fuzz(1024) — runs the function on 1024 random inputs, checking the contract on each generic — every check runs with T=u64; whatever they earn covers only that type trusted (a human vouches for this; no machine checks it): SPSC cross-thread safety (happens-before between cursors) — evidence: loom test tests/loom_spsc.rs 1 worked example(s), each compiled into a test
